matchups.intro: Graco's two best-selling Modes travel systems share a frame and a reversible seat. The differences are the newborn mode, the car seat and the trays.
matchups.bottom_line: Get the Pramette if you want a flat newborn mode without the car seat and a SnugRide 35 that lasts longer. Get the Element for parent and child trays and its higher rating spread.
matchups.choose_a: You'll walk with a newborn without the car seat, or want the 35 lb car seat.
matchups.choose_b: You want trays and a self-standing fold, and will use the car seat for newborn walks.

matchups.intro: The all-in-one car seat stroller versus a light travel stroller that takes a Graco car seat — the two most popular ways to make the car-to-stroller switch easy.
matchups.bottom_line: The Doona is the most convenient setup for year one and on planes, but it's outgrown at 30 lb. The Ready2Jet plus a Graco SnugRide costs less and keeps working as a travel stroller to 50 lb.
matchups.choose_a: You want the fastest car-to-stroller switch and fly often in the first year.
matchups.choose_b: You want a setup that lasts into the toddler years for less money.

matchups.intro: Two single-to-double strollers with a flat newborn option and big baskets — one premium, one value.
matchups.bottom_line: The Vista V3 has the better ride, build and resale value. The ChangeGo includes both a carry-cot and a toddler seat in the box, rides two kids out of the box and can become a wagon.
matchups.choose_a: You want the benchmark premium stroller and plan to keep it for years.
matchups.choose_b: You want more included pieces and the wagon option for less.

matchups.intro: Two newborn-ready strollers with flat pramette modes and reversible seats — one stroller only, one with a car seat included.
matchups.bottom_line: The Wiz is the better value if you already have a car seat or don't need one on the stroller. The Pramette is the better deal if you need a car seat too.
matchups.choose_a: You already have an infant car seat or mostly walk from home.
matchups.choose_b: You want the car seat and base included.

matchups.intro: Two of the lightest strollers on Amazon, both under 12 lb and built for planes.
matchups.bottom_line: The Pockit Air folds smaller and lighter. The Ultra Air has a one-hand fold, a full canopy and a bigger basket, so it doubles better as an everyday stroller.
matchups.choose_a: The smallest, lightest fold is all that matters.
matchups.choose_b: You want a travel stroller you'll also use every day.

matchups.intro: Two travel strollers that both work from birth, in different ways: a near-flat recline versus a Graco car seat.
matchups.bottom_line: The Lithe V2 lets a newborn lie nearly flat without a car seat and includes a rain cover and tray. The Ready2Jet is lighter and takes any Graco SnugRide.
matchups.choose_a: You want your baby to nap flat on the go without a car seat.
matchups.choose_b: You have a Graco SnugRide and want the lightest setup.

matchups.intro: The two jogging strollers most runners shortlist: BOB's classic and Baby Jogger's hand-brake rival.
matchups.bottom_line: The BOB has the better-proven ride and a much larger review base. The Summit X3 adds a hand brake, a one-hand fold and a 75 lb limit for less money.
matchups.choose_a: Ride quality and track record matter most.
matchups.choose_b: You run hills or want an easier fold.

matchups.intro: Premium jogger versus Amazon's best-selling budget jogger.
matchups.bottom_line: The BOB's suspension and air tires are worth it for regular runners and trails. For casual runs and walks on paths, the Expedition delivers most of the experience for a fraction of the price.
matchups.choose_a: You run several times a week or on rough trails.
matchups.choose_b: You jog casually and want to spend under $200.
